evidence: Invite students to say out loud what the moon sees on that page and add it to the What the Moon Sees anchor chart.
rationale: The standard requires students to share relevant and accurate information through a variety of different modes (C). Students share relevant, accurate information about what the moon sees at night: during the close viewing, students turn and talk with partners, contributing observations such as "a raccoon; dark, leafy trees" from photographs and videos, and during the read-aloud they "say out loud what the moon sees on that page." These contributions are recorded on the What the Moon Sees anchor chart, and students also share connections during the Interactive Word Wall protocol using sentence frames like "I connected ___ and ___ because they ___." However, the "variety of different modes" clause is only partially met: the dominant mode is oral (turn-and-talk, partner protocols, whole-group sharing), and the only alternative mode—whiteboards for drawing or writing—is offered as an optional scaffold, not a required activity, capping that clause at partial.
standard_raw_text: Share relevant and accurate information through a variety of different modes. (C)

evidence: 'What do you see in the illustrations that helps you know it is a quiet barnyard?' (Animals are sleeping; the animals are not moving.)
rationale: The lesson meets the interpretation (I) clauses: students build and draw from comprehension skills by answering text-dependent questions during the focused read-aloud ("'What do you see in the illustrations that helps you know it is a quiet barnyard?' (Animals are sleeping; the animals are not moving.)") and by observing and describing photographs/videos during close viewing ("'What could the moon 'see' or observe?' (a raccoon; dark, leafy trees)"). These activities have students actively applying comprehension strategies such as using illustrations as evidence, vocabulary acquisition, and close viewing. However, the construction (C) clauses are not met: students do not compose or construct any text in this lesson. The lesson previews that students will write a class narrative poem "beginning in the next lesson," but no drafting, writing, or other composition act occurs here. The standard's (I/C) tag requires both interpretation and construction for full alignment.
standard_raw_text: Build a repertoire of comprehension and composition skills, strategies, and techniques, drawing from them as needed to aid the interpretation and construction of texts. (I/C)

rationale: The standard requires students to work with others to discuss topics, investigate questions, solve problems, and explore and create texts. Students discuss topics collaboratively: "Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner: 'What could the moon "see" or observe?'" and work in small groups during the Interactive Word Wall protocol connecting vocabulary. Students investigate questions with partners via the Pinky Partners protocol: "'How will our role-play and close viewing of the photographs and videos help you write a story? Students explore the text collaboratively through the Role-Play protocol in pairs, but no collaborative text creation occurs in this lesson (deferred to the next lesson), so the "create texts" component is unmet. evidence: Display night photograph 1 and provide time for students to silently view it. ... Play 'Wildlife in the Backyard at Night.' ... Play 'Downtown Boston at Night.'
rationale: The consume clause is partially met: students engage with multiple modalities — a printed literary text read aloud (What the Sun Sees, What the Moon Sees), night photographs, and video clips ("Wildlife in the Backyard at Night," "Downtown Boston at Night") — and respond to them ("Display night photograph 1 and provide time for students to silently view it"; "Play 'Wildlife in the Backyard at Night'"; students turn and talk about observations). However, the lesson never asks students to attend to or integrate how different genres, text features, or craft techniques function together across those modes; the multimodal consumption is present but the "integrating a variety of genres, text features, and craft techniques" component is only thinly addressed (adjective use is noted as a craft technique in the text but is not connected across modes). The produce clause is not met: no student production of a multimodal text occurs in this lesson; the teacher only previews that students will write a class narrative poem "beginning in the next lesson."
standard_raw_text: Consume and produce multimodal texts, integrating a variety of genres, text features, and craft techniques to influence target audiences and achieve specific purposes. (I/C)
